advances: The first genuine boundary escape from the six-positive common-fan obstruction must lose a \(Q\)-singleton, not merely a \(P\)-doubleton.  More precisely, weighted balance and common-fan convexity exclude every branch in which all three \(Q\)-singletons remain positive, even if some \(P\)-doubletons vanish.  At distance one from the six-positive support, the only surviving patterns are therefore \(q_k=0\) or \(q_\ell=0\) for the two nonopposite indices.  An exact rational scalar table with only \(q_2=0\) passes the crossings, tails, slice balance, all three convex three-cap gates, the general completion filter, the opposite-pair budget, and the forced target-cell Brunn--Minkowski capacities.  A separate exact rational common-fan pair realizes precisely this one-zero support class.  That pair fails the tails and balanced-completion range, so no simultaneous geometric realization of the scalar table is asserted.  The remaining issue is quantitative common-fan cell-mass realizability, not support filling.
author: mp_r381_opposite_threecap_global
proof:
We first strengthen the common-fan obstruction in accepted fact
`0773c759f7f76dd9` on the \(Q\)-side.  Put
\[
\delta=-1-(L_1+L_2+L_3)>0,\qquad
\sigma=\delta+2,
\]
\[
p_i=f_i-L_i,\qquad q_i=f_i+L_i.
\]
The bounded ambient triangles are
\[
\mathcal T_P=\{p_1,p_2,p_3\geq0\},
\qquad
\mathcal T_Q=\{q_1,q_2,q_3\leq0\}.
\]
The \(Q\)-containment argument in the proof of accepted fact
`0773c759f7f76dd9` uses only \(q_1,q_2,q_3>0\), not the
\(P\)-doubleton hypotheses.  Indeed, the affine coordinates
\[
x_i=-\frac{q_i}{\sigma},\qquad x_1+x_2+x_3=1,
\]
map a strict point of \(Q_i\) to a point whose \(i\)-th coordinate is
greater than \(1\) and whose other two coordinates are negative.
The nonnegative-inverse barycentric argument from that accepted fact
then puts all three standard basis vectors in the image of \(A_2\).
Hence
\[
\mathcal T_Q\subseteq A_2,
\qquad
q_{123}=|\mathcal T_Q|.
\tag{15}
\]
No assumption on \(P_{12},P_{13},P_{23}\) was used.

The cell \(P_0\) is always contained in \(\mathcal T_P\), so
\[
p_0\leq|\mathcal T_P|.
\tag{16}
\]
The exact common-Jacobian calculation in accepted fact
`0773c759f7f76dd9` gives
\[
\frac{|\mathcal T_Q|}{|\mathcal T_P|}
=\left(\frac{\delta+2}{\delta}\right)^2>1.
\tag{17}
\]
Thus all three positive \(Q\)-singletons would imply
\[
q_{123}>p_0.
\tag{18}
\]

On the other hand, accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f` gives
\(P_{123}=Q_0=R_0=\varnothing\).  Therefore the only negative
coefficient in \(W\) is the coefficient \(-2\) of \(p_0\).
All other coefficients are nonnegative, and the coefficient of
\(q_{123}\) is \(7\).  From \(W=0\),
\[
2p_0\geq7q_{123}.
\tag{19}
\]
Equations (18)--(19) are incompatible.  This proves (1).
Under (2), \(q_j>0\), so the missing singleton supplied by (1) is
\(q_k\) or \(q_\ell\).  If exactly one member of (3) vanishes, it is
therefore one of those two \(Q\)-singletons.  The four-path
classification in accepted fact `a2a9387275a2c97c`, with the outer
path through the missing singleton deleted, gives exactly (4).
This also refines the filling conclusion of accepted fact
`78d1d57e3961c4e4`.

We now audit the scalar survivor.  The rows (5)--(7) sum respectively
to the three totals in (8).  Define
\[
u_i=\sum_{J\ni i}p_J,\qquad
v_i=\sum_{J\ni i}q_J,\qquad
b_i=\sum_{J\ni i}r_J,\qquad
d_i=u_i+v_i.
\]
Direct rational summation gives
\[
u=
\left(
\frac{129}{4600},
\frac{1324829}{11500000},
\frac{975171}{11500000}
\right),
\tag{20}
\]
\[
v=
\left(
\frac{1021}{3450},
\frac{169}{4600},
\frac{129}{2300}
\right),
\tag{21}
\]
\[
d=
\left(
\frac{4471}{13800},
\frac{1747329}{11500000},
\frac{1620171}{11500000}
\right),
\tag{22}
\]
\[
b=
\left(
\frac{1691}{13800},
\frac{3387671}{11500000},
\frac{3514829}{11500000}
\right).
\tag{23}
\]
Since
\[
\frac{2(M+m+\kappa)}9=\frac{1027}{2300},
\]
(22)--(23) give all three crossings
\[
d_i+b_i=\frac{1027}{2300}\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\tag{24}
\]
They also imply \(W=0\), because
\[
W=3\sum_i(d_i+b_i)-2(M+m+\kappa)=0.
\]

For the canonical tails of accepted fact `624b129b68e0fdee`, the
crossings reduce the two tail conditions to \(d_i\leq m\) and
\(d_i<M\).  Here both are strict, and the smallest left-tail margin is
\[
m-\max_i d_i
=\frac13-\frac{4471}{13800}
=\frac{43}{4600}
=\varepsilon.
\tag{25}
\]
All endpoint and middle cap masses are strictly between zero and their
ambient totals.

Apply accepted fact `5b75ecd9ec86dbcf` separately to the three formal
cell tables.  For \(A_0\), the three relevant cap masses are
\(M-u_i\); for \(A_2\), they are \(v_i\); and for \(K\), they are
\(b_i\).  Their exact residuals are
\[
5\sum_i(M-u_i)-6\min_i(M-u_i)-4M
=\frac{26168237}{5750000}>0,
\tag{26}
\]
\[
5\sum_i v_i-6\min_i v_i-4m
=\frac{5383}{13800}>0,
\tag{27}
\]
\[
5\sum_i b_i-6\min_i b_i-4\kappa
=\frac{301}{1725}>0.
\tag{28}
\]
Thus all three nonconcurrent three-cap gates hold strictly.

The strict slice balances used with accepted fact
`2f9be517307232c7` follow from
\[
\kappa-(M-m)=\frac{43}{4600}>0,
\qquad
M+m-\kappa=\frac{9071}{13800}>0,
\tag{29}
\]
and \(m<M+\kappa\).  Moreover
\[
\frac38-\frac mM=\frac1{24}>0.
\tag{30}
\]

The maximum endpoint cap sum in (22) is \(d_1\).  Substitution into
the general completion filter of accepted fact
`a7747c32a219e2c9` gives the strict margin
\[
\begin{aligned}
&M+m-k_0-\frac52(d_1+d_2+d_3)+3d_1-A\\
&\qquad=\frac{301}{3450}>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{31}
\]
The ordinary compatibility Brunn--Minkowski bound also holds:
\[
k_0>
\frac14\left(1+\frac1{\sqrt3}\right)^2.
\tag{32}
\]
Indeed, \(\sqrt3>5/3\), so the right side of (32) is less than
\(16/25\), while
\[
k_0-\frac{16}{25}=\frac2{75}>0.
\]

It remains to check the genuinely opposite-pair capacities rather
than only their aggregate total.  The two endpoint terms in accepted
fact `9922bcace1cdc113` are
\[
\Phi_3=
\frac14\left(\sqrt{\frac45}+\sqrt{\frac1{50}}\right)^2
=\frac{41}{200}+\frac{\sqrt{10}}{50},
\tag{33}
\]
\[
\Phi_{12}=
\frac14\left(\sqrt{\frac45}+\sqrt{\frac1{100}}\right)^2
=\frac{81}{400}+\frac{\sqrt5}{50}.
\tag{34}
\]
Use the rational strict upper bounds
\[
\Phi_3<\frac{134123}{500000}=:E_3,
\qquad
\Phi_{12}<\frac{123611}{500000}=:E_{12}.
\tag{35}
\]
They have exact square certificates
\[
31623^2-10\cdot10000^2=14129>0,
\qquad
22361^2-5\cdot10000^2=14321>0.
\tag{36}
\]

The forced single-cell incidence in accepted fact
`0e51a47a9add571f` and the opposite-support accounting in accepted
fact `a2a9387275a2c97c` require the first endpoint image to fit in
\(R_3\), the second to fit in
\(R_1\cup R_2\cup R_{12}\), and the slab to fit in
\(R_{13}\cup R_{23}\cup R_{123}\).  The exact capacity margins are
\[
r_3-E_3=\frac{43}{4600}>0,
\tag{37}
\]
\[
r_1+r_2+r_{12}-E_{12}
=\frac{2124427}{17250000}>0,
\tag{38}
\]
\[
r_{13}+r_{23}+r_{123}-s_3
=\frac{43}{4600}>0.
\tag{39}
\]
The corresponding reservation inside the compatible midpoint body
also has room:
\[
k_0-E_3-E_{12}-s_3
=\frac{2285677}{17250000}>0.
\tag{40}
\]
Finally, the weighted opposite-pair budget from accepted fact
`a2a9387275a2c97c` has the stronger rational slack
\[
2p_0-
\left(q_3+4q_{12}+E_3+E_{12}+4s_3\right)
=\frac{5461059}{5750000}>0.
\tag{41}
\]
Equations (35) and (37)--(41) therefore imply all the same strict
inequalities with the exact radical terms (33)--(34).  The required
filling is also strict:
\[
q_{13}+q_{23}+q_{123}
=\frac{83}{2300}>0.
\tag{42}
\]
This proves every claimed scalar property.

For the common-fan support realization, the functions in (10) have
pairwise nonparallel linear parts and sum to \(-1\), while
\(\sum_iL_i=-2<-1\).  Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_1&=-6X+\frac43,&
p_2&=-3Y+\frac43,&
p_3&=6X+3Y-\frac53,\\
q_1&=-6X,&
q_2&=-3Y,&
q_3&=6X+3Y-3.
\end{aligned}
\tag{43}
\]
Clipping the triangle and rectangle in (11) by the six rational lines
in (43), then applying the shoelace formula to each clipped polygon,
gives exactly (12)--(13).  Their row sums are
\[
\frac1{36}+3\frac{55}{324}+3\frac{25}{162}=1,
\qquad
\frac{47+24+49+25+24+23}{576}=\frac13.
\]
Every entry other than \(q_2\) is positive.  Hence this is an exact
rational common-fan realization of the minimal one-zero support class,
and the opposite cells \(p_0,q_3,q_{12}\) are positive.

For completeness, exact Minkowski addition and rational clipping give
\[
u_1=u_2=u_3=\frac{155}{324},
\qquad
v=\left(\frac14,\frac16,\frac16\right),
\]
so
\[
d=
\left(\frac{59}{81},\frac{209}{324},\frac{209}{324}\right).
\tag{44}
\]
All three coordinates in (44) exceed \(m=1/3\), violating the left
tails.  The same exact Minkowski sum has area \(11/8\), proving (14);
therefore every \(K\) containing it violates the strict balanced-slice
upper bound \(|K|<M+m=4/3\).  This proves only that the support class is
geometrically genuine.  It neither realizes the scalar masses
(5)--(7) nor excludes a different common-fan realization satisfying
the tails and completion gates.

SageMath \(10.8\) checked all rational sums, cap vectors, crossings,
orders, tail margins, three-cap residuals, completion margins, clipped
cell areas, Minkowski area, and the square certificates in
(20)--(44) over \(\mathbb Q\).  Wolfram Language \(14.3\) independently
found (5)--(9) by exact rational linear optimization after enumerating
the cap-order branches.  No floating-point feasibility decision is
used in the stated certificates.
statement:
Use the exact-cell convention of accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f`.
Let
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1,\qquad L_1+L_2+L_3<-1,
\]
let \(A_0,A_2,K\) be compact two-dimensional convex bodies with
\((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq K\), and write
\[
p_J=|P_J|,\qquad q_J=|Q_J|,\qquad r_J=|R_J|.
\]
Put
\[
W=
\sum_J(3|J|-2)p_J+
\sum_J(3|J|-2)q_J+
\sum_J(3|J|-2)r_J.
\]
If \(W=0\), then
\[
q_1q_2q_3=0.
\tag{1}
\]
Consequently, in a positive opposite-pair branch
\[
p_0q_jq_{\{k,\ell\}}>0,\qquad \{j,k,\ell\}=\{1,2,3\},
\tag{2}
\]
at least one of \(q_k,q_\ell\) vanishes.  In particular, a boundary
pattern in which the only vanished member of
\[
\{p_{12},p_{13},p_{23},q_1,q_2,q_3\}
\tag{3}
\]
is a \(P\)-doubleton is impossible.  Up to interchanging \(k,\ell\),
the first one-zero boundary class has \(q_\ell=0\), while the other
five masses in (3) are positive.  Its connected positive \(Q\)-support
contains one of the surviving paths
\[
\{j,jk,k,k\ell\},\qquad
\{j,jk,123,k\ell\},\qquad
\{j,j\ell,123,k\ell\}.
\tag{4}
\]

This one-zero class is not excluded by the full scalar relaxation.
Fix
\[
(j,k,\ell)=(3,1,2),\qquad
\varepsilon=\frac{43}{4600},
\]
and assign the endpoint cells
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
J&0&1&2&3&12&13&23\\ \hline
p_J&
\frac45&
\frac{43}{4600}&
\frac{1109829}{11500000}&
\frac{760171}{11500000}&
\frac{43}{4600}&
\frac{43}{4600}&
\frac{43}{4600}
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
and
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
J&1&2&3&12&13&23&123\\ \hline
q_J&
\frac{461}{1725}&
0&
\frac1{50}&
\frac1{100}&
\frac{43}{4600}&
\frac2{115}&
\frac{43}{4600}.
\end{array}
\tag{6}
\]
Assign the formal middle cells
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
J&1&2&3&12&13&23&123\\ \hline
r_J&
\frac{163}{1725}&
\frac{3065171}{11500000}&
\frac{3192329}{11500000}&
\frac{43}{4600}&
\frac{43}{4600}&
\frac{43}{4600}&
\frac{43}{4600}.
\end{array}
\tag{7}
\]
Then
\[
M=1,\qquad m=\frac13,\qquad
\kappa=\frac{9329}{13800},\qquad
k_0=\frac23,\qquad
A=\kappa-k_0=\varepsilon.
\tag{8}
\]
Every non-forced cell except \(q_2\) is positive, and every displayed
positive cell is at least \(\varepsilon\).  With the formal slab
allocation
\[
s_3=\frac{43}{2300}=2\varepsilon,
\tag{9}
\]
the table passes all the scalar gates listed in the proof, including
the forced-cell capacities for the two opposite endpoint images and
the slab.

The support class of (5)--(6) is itself exactly realizable by rational
common-fan polygons with the same totals \(M=1,m=1/3\).  In coordinates
\((X,Y)\), take
\[
\begin{aligned}
f_1&=-6X+\frac23,\\
f_2&=-3Y+\frac23,\\
f_3&=6X+3Y-\frac73,
\end{aligned}
\qquad
L_1=L_2=L_3=-\frac23,
\tag{10}
\]
\[
A_0=\operatorname{conv}
\left\{
\left(-\frac12,1\right),
\left(\frac12,-1\right),
\left(\frac12,1\right)
\right\},
\qquad
A_2=
\left[-\frac12,\frac32\right]
\times
\left[-\frac1{12},\frac1{12}\right].
\tag{11}
\]
Its exact endpoint cell masses are
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
J&0&1&2&3&12&13&23\\ \hline
p_J&
\frac1{36}&
\frac{55}{324}&
\frac{55}{324}&
\frac{55}{324}&
\frac{25}{162}&
\frac{25}{162}&
\frac{25}{162}
\end{array}
\tag{12}
\]
and
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
J&1&2&3&12&13&23&123\\ \hline
q_J&
\frac{47}{576}&
0&
\frac1{24}&
\frac{49}{576}&
\frac{25}{576}&
\frac1{24}&
\frac{23}{576}.
\end{array}
\tag{13}
\]
Thus only \(q_2\) vanishes among all non-forced endpoint cells.
This particular support realization is not a full survivor: its
endpoint cap sums violate the canonical tails, and
\[
\left|\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\right|=\frac{11}{8}>\frac43=M+m.
\tag{14}
\]
